The test `BugCLI162Test.testLongLineChunkingIndentIgnored()` is failing due to an infinite loop in the wrapping code of the `HelpFormatter` class. The issue occurs when there is not enough space to display a word on a single line, causing `HelpFormatter` to go into an infinite loop until the JVM crashes with an `OutOfMemoryError`.

In the test method, various options are set up, and then the `HelpFormatter` prints the help information using the `printHelp` method with specific parameters. The `printHelp` method is responsible for printing the help information with the specified command line syntax, header, and footer.

Looking at the implementation of the `printHelp` method in the `HelpFormatter` class, we see that it calls another overloaded version of `printHelp` with additional parameters, including a boolean flag. However, the infinite loop issue seems to be related to the formatting logic within the `printHelp` method itself.

To address this issue, you should investigate the logic within the `printHelp` method of the `HelpFormatter` class to identify the part that causes the infinite loop. This loop may be related to how the text is wrapped or handled when there is limited space for displaying the information.

Suggested Fix:
```java
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printHelp(int, java.lang.String, java.lang.String, org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String)
```
